chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

When you shroud the deceased, then sprinkle on each cloth some dharirah and camphor, and place some of the hanut upon his points of hearing and his places of prostration, and some upon the outer side of the shroud.

key_terms.الْحَنُوطِ: the funerary perfume mixture applied to the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared for burial
key_terms.ذَرِيرَةٍ: a perfumed powder or fragrant substance sprinkled in the shrouding process
key_terms.كَفَّنْتَ: you shrouded the deceased in the burial cloth
key_terms.مَسَاجِدِهِ: his places of sajdah, meaning the bodily points associated with prostration
key_terms.مَسَامِعِهِ: his organs or areas of hearing

ai.seo_question: How should camphor and hanut be applied when shrouding the deceased in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling concerning the preparation of the deceased for burial. It instructs that dharirah and camphor be applied to the shroud and that hanut be placed on specific parts of the body and on the back of the shroud.
